topics.topic: India’s Resilient Production Systems in Agriculture
topics.why_in_news: PIB highlighted record foodgrain and horticulture production, rising agri exports and policy focus on climate-resilient and technology-driven agriculture systems in India.
prelims_quick_notes: India recorded 357.73 MMT foodgrain production in 2024–25.
Climate-resilient agriculture focuses on sustainability and diversification.
Millets promoted as low-water climate-resilient crops.
PMFBY supports crop insurance and climate risk mitigation.
10,000 FPOs strengthen collective bargaining and value chains.
Natural farming promoted to reduce chemical dependency.
key_findings_and_indicators: Agri exports increased to USD 51.1 billion.
Food processing employs significant manufacturing workforce share.
important_facts: India among largest producers of millets, pulses and spices.
e-NAM is pan-India digital agricultural market platform.
PMFBY covers natural disasters, pests and diseases.
exam_relevance: Important for Agriculture, Economy and Food Security.
Useful for climate resilience, agri reforms and rural economy topics.
Can be linked with sustainable agriculture, SDGs and farmer welfare.
prelims_traps: Horticulture output now exceeds foodgrain production.
LFPR and agricultural employment are different indicators.
PMFBY is insurance scheme, not direct income support.
ONORC relates to food security portability under NFSA.

topics.topic: India – New Zealand Free Trade Agreement
topics.why_in_news: India and New Zealand signed a comprehensive Free Trade Agreement providing duty-free access, investment commitments and mobility provisions to strengthen bilateral trade and economic cooperation.
prelims_quick_notes: FTA provides 100% duty-free access for Indian exports.
India protects sensitive sectors like dairy and edible oils.
FTA includes investment commitment of USD 20 billion.
Mobility provisions introduced for skilled professionals and students.
Focus on MSMEs, labour-intensive sectors and services trade.
Rules of Origin included to prevent trade diversion.
GI protection provisions included for Indian products.
key_findings_and_indicators: Bilateral trade increased from USD 873 million to USD 1.3 billion.
India signed FTAs with multiple developed countries recently.
Textiles, leather and engineering sectors expected to benefit.
important_facts: India excludes dairy sector from liberalisation.
TRQs used for select agricultural products.
Rules of Origin prevent misuse of tariff benefits.
MFN treatment provided in multiple service sectors.
GI protection includes products like Basmati and Darjeeling tea.
FTA strengthens India’s Oceania and Indo-Pacific outreach.
exam_relevance: Important for Economy, Trade and International Relations.
Useful for FTAs, supply chains and export competitiveness topics.
Can be linked with Indo-Pacific strategy and economic diplomacy.
prelims_traps: India did not open all agricultural sectors under FTA.
Rules of Origin are critical in FTAs to prevent trade diversion.
TRQs differ from complete tariff elimination.
FTA includes both goods and services provisions.
